bull_bear.body:
- Modern manufacturing facility - 32,780.88 sq ft, fully automated from raw material handling to finished product packaging with minimal human intervention, real-time monitoring and technologies sourced from China
- Dual-channel distribution of personal health and hygiene products - General Trade networks plus major e-commerce platforms, covering B2B and B2C
- Brand affinity, loyalty and trust - Femiss won the National Award for Excellence in Healthcare 2020 for 'Best Emerging Brand of the Year', Business Leadership Award 2021 for 'Innovative Product - Feminine Hygiene Ultrafluff Sanitary Pad', and 'Best Hypoallergenic Hygiene and Sanitary Brand of the Year 2025'
- Wide geographic presence in India - more than 227 customers across 28 states and 8 union territories over the last three Fiscals
- Quality and compliance credentials - ISO 9001:2015, WHO-GMP and BIS certifications with a 5-member quality team as on May 31, 2026
- Long-standing customer relationships - five customers associated with the Company for more than 5 years
- Multi-brand portfolio spanning the hygiene care spectrum from babies (Bloom Baby) to young women (Femiss, Womanica) to the elderly (ElderFit)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Severe customer concentration — Top ten customers were 80.41% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 (78.32% in Fiscal 2025, 79.57% in Fiscal 2024); Customer 1 alone contributed 6,320.81 lakhs or 48.35% in Fiscal 2026, up from 34.16% in Fiscal 2025
- Dependence on a government order executed as a third-party contractor — For Customer 1 - the single largest customer at 48.35% of Fiscal 2026 revenue - the Company is a third party contractor executing work for a government order in Fiscals 2026 and 2025, making the largest revenue block non-recurring in nature
- Geographic concentration in Western India — Western India was 84.42% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations with Gujarat the dominant market; Northern India revenue fell from 2,749.62 lakhs (32.60%) in Fiscal 2024 to 565.08 lakhs (4.32%) in Fiscal 2026
- Single manufacturing facility — All manufacturing is concentrated at one Rajkot, Gujarat facility of 32,780.88 sq ft; any disruption there would halt production across all brands
- Dependence on imported plant technology — The facility incorporates technologies majorly sourced from China, creating exposure to import, spares, servicing and trade-policy disruption
- Outstanding legal proceedings across the Company, Group Company, Promoters, Directors and KMP/SMP — Proceedings pending at different levels of adjudication could divert management time and financial resources, and an adverse judgment could adversely affect business, financial condition and results of operations
- Change in statutory auditor shortly before the offer — The erstwhile statutory auditor resigned due to pre-occupation in other assignments w.e.f. April 21, 2026 and Savjani & Associates was appointed against the casual vacancy; future auditor changes or transition disruption may affect timely statutory audits, financial reporting and regulatory filings
- Industry data is from a commissioned, non-independently-verified report — Industry and market information is derived from the Credence Research Report, which was commissioned and paid for by the Company for an agreed fee and has not been independently verified

outlook.body: The Company began production in 2017-18 with an initial capacity of approximately 4 lakh units per day, launched Femiss and Womanica in 2018-19, extended distribution to North and East India in 2019-20, commenced online sales in 2022-23 and in 2023-24 added a new manufacturing line (stated in the RHP as a capacity of approximately 8 Crore pieces per day), taking installed capacity at the single Rajkot facility to 6.41 lakh sanitary napkins/pieces per day across 32,780.88 sq ft. Production volumes grew from 11.40 crore pieces per annum in Fiscal 2024 to 18.15 crore pieces per annum in Fiscal 2025, and property, plant and equipment additions of Rs 44.89, Rs 34.68 lakhs and Rs 565.23 lakhs in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 cumulatively constitute about 51.12% of gross block as of March 31, 2026. The next expansion step is a second manufacturing facility at Rajkot, Gujarat ("Proposed facility Unit 2"), to be funded with Rs 3,136.12 lakhs of Net Proceeds from the Fresh Offer; the product range was also broadened into adult diapers (ElderFit, December 2024) and baby diapers (Bloom Baby, April 2025).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Raw material and supply chain vulnerability - the RHP identifies supply chain disruption as a combined factor affecting results of operations
- Revenue mix shift from white-label manufacturing to own brands - own brand rose from 5.37% of revenue in Fiscal 2024 to 79.06% in Fiscal 2025 and 94.47% in Fiscal 2026, while white labelling fell from 61.08% to 3.00%
- Channel mix between offline distributors (92.79% of FY2026 revenue) and e-commerce (7.21%), with Meesho the dominant online platform
- Customer concentration - top ten customers accounted for 80.41%, 78.32% and 79.57% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, with Customer 1 alone at 48.35% in Fiscal 2026
- Geographic concentration in Western India (84.42% of FY2026 revenue), with Gujarat the dominant market
- Operating leverage from a largely automated single facility - EBITDA margin improved from 8.98% (FY2024) to 12.88% (FY2025) and 13.07% (FY2026)
- Deleveraging - debt to equity fell from 4.19x (FY2024) to 0.67x (FY2025) and 0.51x (FY2026), while RoE fell from 126.65% to 30.90% on a larger equity base
- Working capital cycle - net capital turnover ratio declined from 8.81x (FY2024) to 5.22x (FY2025) and 3.18x (FY2026); current ratio 1.41x in FY2026

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward: major raw materials are fluff pulp and superabsorbent polymers (plus top sheet, back sheet, tissue paper, air-laid paper, wing release paper and glue), sourced from suppliers in the U.S. and India. Imported raw material purchases fell from Rs 2,370.42 lakhs (46.62% of purchases) in Fiscal 2024 to Rs 1,541.23 lakhs (38.60%) in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 318.54 lakhs (5.74%) in Fiscal 2026, with domestic sourcing rising to 94.26%; total raw material purchases were Rs 5,553.17 lakhs in Fiscal 2026. The Company sourced from 88, 78 and 62 suppliers in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, does not enter into agreements with suppliers, and states that 4 of its top 10 suppliers have been associated with it for about 3 years; materials consumed were 46.24%, 42.11% and 46.30% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Manufacturing is in-house at the owned, fully automated Rajkot unit (raw material handling through to finished-product packaging), though 48.58% of Fiscal 2026 revenue came from the Trading segment rather than own manufacturing. Forward: own-brand portfolio (Femiss, Womanica, ElderFit, Bloom Baby) plus white-label manufacture, distributed pan-India through a dual-channel model - 25 Consignment Sale Agents servicing approximately 202 distributors with a sales and marketing team of over 99 personnel (offline 92.79% of Fiscal 2026 revenue), and direct e-commerce presence on Meesho, Amazon, Flipkart, Glowroad, Snapdeal, JioMart and Myntra (online 7.21%, of which Meesho alone was 6.83%). Customer base of more than 227 customers across 28 states and 8 union territories. The DRHP notes that for Customer 1 (48.35% of Fiscal 2026 revenue and 34.16% of Fiscal 2025 revenue) the Company acts as a third-party contractor executing work for a government order.

opportunities: Diaper packets sold scaled from Nil (FY2024) to 2,75,880 (FY2025) to 424,110 (FY2026), indicating a recently added product line with room to scale off a small base.

The Company's stated Pan India presence and Dual Channel Strategy position it for the DRHP-described shift of hygiene product distribution toward e-commerce, quick commerce and Direct-to-Consumer models.

The DRHP describes regulatory measures such as BIS certification for sanitary products reshaping the market toward quality and safety; the Company's stated BIS, WHO-GMP and ISO 9001:2015 certifications align it with that tightening standard regime.

The DRHP describes rural and Tier 2/Tier 3 adoption of hygiene products as still relatively low, and adult diapers and eco-friendly/biodegradable formats as expanding categories, representing addressable segments adjacent to the Company's existing products.
strengths: State-of-the-art production facility spread across 32,780.88 sq. ft., equipped with fully automated systems spanning raw material handling to finished product packaging (stated qualitative factor).
Distribution of personal health & hygiene products through a Dual Channel Strategy (stated qualitative factor).
Brand affinity, loyalty and trust of customers in the Company's brands (stated qualitative factor).
Facility certifications include ISO 9001:2015, WHO-GMP and BIS, with stated focus on quality control and assurance systems to ensure compliance with applicable health and hygiene standards.
Revenue from Operations rose across the disclosed period: Rs 8,434.76 lakhs (FY2024), Rs 11,462.56 lakhs (FY2025), Rs 13,072.09 lakhs (FY2026); stated Revenue CAGR 24.49%.
PAT rose across the disclosed period: Rs 466.41 lakhs (FY2024), Rs 908.10 lakhs (FY2025), Rs 1,140.66 lakhs (FY2026).
EBITDA margin expanded over the disclosed period: 8.98% (FY2024), 12.88% (FY2025), 13.07% (FY2026).
Debt to Equity Ratio reduced over the disclosed period: 4.19 times (FY2024), 0.67 times (FY2025), 0.51 times (FY2026).
Net Fixed Asset Turnover Ratio improved over the disclosed period: 10.30 times (FY2024), 16.02 times (FY2025), 20.40 times (FY2026).
threats: Competitive Rivalry assessed as 'High': the DRHP names global players P&G, Unicharm and Kimberly-Clark and local brands Nobel Hygiene and Redcliffe Hygiene Private Limited competing for share.
Product categories such as sanitary pads, diapers and wipes are described as saturated with similar offerings, making differentiation beyond price, comfort and branding difficult.
Rise of D2C brands has intensified competition, especially in urban areas where brand switching is common due to low switching costs.
Buyer Power assessed as 'Moderate to High', with consumers having wide brand/format/pricing choice across offline and online channels and low switching costs.
Threat of New Entrants assessed as 'Moderate', with barriers to entry described as relatively low in commodity segments such as low-cost sanitary pads.

Threat of Substitutes assessed as 'Moderate', including traditional alternatives (cloth, ash, washable nappies) in lower-income and rural areas and reusable menstrual cups and cloth diapers among eco-conscious urban users.
Government-subsidised Suvidha sanitary pads priced at Rs 1 per pad are described as making menstrual hygiene affordable on a mass scale, indicating price pressure at the low end of the category.
Environmental and disposal concerns around non-biodegradable sanitary pads and diapers, with associated regulatory attention to biodegradable standards and sanitary waste management.

Supplier Power assessed as 'Low to Moderate', but the DRHP notes reliance on imports for certain key inputs, especially high-quality or biodegradable materials, can increase costs and reduce bargaining power.
Cultural taboos and societal stigma around menstruation, and limited rural access due to fragmented supply chains and last-mile delivery challenges, constrain category adoption.
weaknesses: The DRHP itself states there are no listed Indian companies in its business segment or of comparable size, so the document provides no peer accounting-ratio benchmark against which the Offer Price can be assessed.
Volume concentration in sanitary napkins: 18,13,00,285 packets sold in FY2026 versus 424,110 diaper packets, with diaper packets sold reported as Nil in FY2024.
Return on Net worth (RoNW) declined over the disclosed period: 79.11% (FY2024), 28.89% (FY2025), 26.91% (FY2026); weighted average 36.27%.
Return on Equity (RoE) declined over the disclosed period: 126.65% (FY2024), 48.65% (FY2025), 30.90% (FY2026).

Return on Assets declined from 10.03% (FY2025) to 6.67% (FY2026).
Current Ratio eased from 1.71 times (FY2025) to 1.41 times (FY2026).
The qualitative factors describe a single production facility (32,780.88 sq. ft.), indicating manufacturing concentrated at one location.

overview.business_model: The Company manufactures hygiene products at one owned facility at Rajkot (32,780.88 sq ft, installed capacity 6.41 lakh sanitary napkins/pieces per day as on the date of the RHP) and earns revenue in two streams: own-brand sales (Femiss for the economy segment, Womanica premium high-absorbency, ElderFit for the elderly, Bloom Baby for baby care) and white-label manufacture of sanitary napkins for a few customers. Own Brand contributed ₹12,349.82 Lakhs (94.47% of revenue from operations) in FY2026 versus ₹453.14 Lakhs (5.37%) in FY2024, while White Labelling fell from ₹5,151.58 Lakhs (61.08%) in FY2024 to ₹392.74 Lakhs (3.00%) in FY2026. Goods are sold pan-India to B2B and B2C customers through a dual-channel strategy — an offline dealer/distributor network (approximately 202 distributors, 25 Consignment Sale Agents, a sales and marketing team of over 99 personnel as of March 31, 2026) and e-commerce platforms including Meesho, Amazon, Glowroad, Flipkart, Snapdeal and JioMart. 25 SKUs as on May 31, 2026; more than 227 customers across 28 states and 8 union territories for the period ended March 31, 2026, with Western India contributing 84.42% of FY2026 revenue from operations.

financial_valuation.evidence: As of May 31, 2026, insured assets were ₹5,885.14 lakhs and insurance cover as a percentage of total insurable assets was 98.00%.
financial_valuation.title: Insurance coverage may not adequately protect against all material hazards

financial_valuation.detail: The Company carries contingent liabilities for which no provision has been made, comprising a guarantee given on its behalf under the EPCG Scheme for fulfilment of export obligations plus other commitments in respect of Income Tax and TDS. Management expects no material outflow on the EPCG guarantee as it intends to fulfil the stipulated export obligations and considers crystallisation remote, but if any of these contingent liabilities materialise, results of operations and financial condition may be adversely affected.
financial_valuation.title: Contingent liabilities not provided for

financial_valuation.detail: The Company has availed unsecured loans from certain lenders which may be recalled at any time. If any lender seeks repayment, the Company would need alternative sources of financing which may not be available on commercially reasonable terms or at all, affecting liquidity. Inability to procure such financing could leave inadequate working capital to maintain the desired inventory level.
financial_valuation.evidence: Outstanding unsecured loan of ₹941.04 lakhs as on June 30, 2026 (see 'Financial Indebtedness', page 231).
financial_valuation.title: Unsecured loans can be recalled by lenders at any time

financial_valuation.detail: Under the MSME Act, buyers must pay MSME suppliers within prescribed timelines, failing which interest becomes payable at specified rates. Any delay or default in payment to MSME creditors may result in additional interest liabilities, penalties, claims, disputes or legal proceedings initiated by such creditors, and suppliers may approach the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council or other competent authorities for recovery, which may result in litigation, adverse orders or reputational harm. There is no assurance the Company will not experience delays in future.
financial_valuation.evidence: As of March 31, 2026, outstanding dues payable to 54 creditors registered as MSMEs of ₹2,661.21 lakhs. (Trade payables ageing, FY2024-25: MSME 2,924.28 less than 1 year, 10.15 in 1-2 years, 42.44 in 2-3 years, total 2,976.87; others 337.59; total trade payables 3,314.46. FY2023-24: MSME 1,102.32 / 257.66 / 0.36, total 1,360.33; others 129.71; total trade payables 1,490.04.)
financial_valuation.title: Outstanding dues payable to MSME-registered creditors

financial_valuation.detail: The Price Band is based on various factors and assumptions and will be determined by the Company in consultation with the Lead Managers; the Offer Price will be determined through the Book Building Process based on numerous factors described under 'Basis for Offer Price' and may not be indicative of the market price after the Offer. Factors affecting the market price include broad market trends, post-listing financial performance and results, and other factors beyond the Company's control. There is no assurance that an active market will develop or that sustained trading will take place.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'the current market price of securities listed pursuant to certain previous initial public offerings managed by the Lead Managers is below their respective issue price' — see 'Other Regulatory and Statutory Disclosures – Price information of past issues handled by the Lead Managers', page 273; 'Basis for Offer Price', page 100.
financial_valuation.title: Price Band and Offer Price may not be indicative of the post-Offer market price

financial_valuation.detail: Funding requirements are based on management estimates and current business plans and have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution. Deployment of the Net Proceeds will be at the discretion of the Board. Estimates or business plans may have to be reconsidered due to factors beyond the Company's control such as interest rate fluctuations, changes in input cost and inability to identify suitable locations on favourable terms. Prospective investors must rely on management judgement with respect to the use of proceeds, and inability to deploy proceeds in a timely or efficient manner may affect business and results.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Our funding requirements are based on management estimates and our current business plans and has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution' (see 'Objects of the Offer', page 87).
financial_valuation.title: Funding requirements and deployment of Net Proceeds are not appraised by any independent agency

financial_valuation.detail: The Offer consists of a Fresh Offer and an Offer for Sale. The Promoter Selling Shareholders will be entitled to the net proceeds of the Offer for Sale (proceeds net of the Offer Expenses shared by them), and the Company will not receive any of those proceeds.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'The Offer for Sale comprises 20.00 %^ of the total Offer size.' ^Subject to basis of Allotment.
financial_valuation.title: The Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer for Sale

financial_valuation.detail: As on the date of the RHP the Company has not made any alternate arrangements for meeting capital requirements for the objects of the Offer, and has not identified any alternate source of funding. Capital requirements are met through owned funds and internal accruals; any shortfall in net owned funds, internal accruals or inability to raise debt in future would leave capital requirements unmet. Any failure or delay in raising money from the Offer, or any shortfall in Offer Proceeds, may delay the implementation schedule and adversely affect growth plans.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'As on date, we have not made any alternate arrangements for meeting our capital requirements for the objects of the Offer... Further we have not identified any alternate source of funding' (see 'Objects of the Offer', page 87).
financial_valuation.title: No alternate arrangements or identified alternate source of financing for the Objects of the Offer

financial_valuation.detail: Under SEBI LODR Regulations and other applicable provisions, no variation in the utilisation of Net Proceeds as disclosed can be undertaken without shareholder approval through a special resolution, which may not be obtained in a timely manner or at all. Delay or inability in obtaining such approval may adversely affect business or operations and delay deployment of funds as per the disclosed implementation schedule, restricting the Company's ability to respond to changes in business or financial condition by redeploying unutilised proceeds.
financial_valuation.evidence: Utilisation is set out in 'Objects of the Offer' on page 87; variation requires a special resolution of shareholders under SEBI LODR Regulations.
financial_valuation.title: Any variation in the utilisation of Net Proceeds requires prior Shareholders' approval

financial_valuation.detail: The Company may retain all future earnings for use in operations and expansion and may not declare dividends in the foreseeable future. Any determination as to declaration and payment of dividends is at the discretion of the Board and depends on results of operations, financial condition, cash requirements, business prospects, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other financing arrangements. Realisation of a gain by shareholders may therefore depend largely on appreciation in the price of the Equity Shares, which is not assured.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'We may retain all our future earnings, if any, for use in the operations and expansion of our business. As a result, we may not declare dividends in the foreseeable future.' (see 'Dividend Policy', page 180).
financial_valuation.title: Ability to pay dividends depends on future earnings, cash flows and restrictive covenants

financial_valuation.detail: Any instance of disinvestment of equity shares by the Promoters or by other significant shareholders may significantly affect the trading price of the Equity Shares, and the market price may be adversely affected even by a perception or belief that such sales might occur.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Any instance of disinvestments of equity shares by our Promoters or by other significant shareholder(s) may significantly affect the trading price of our Equity Shares.'
financial_valuation.title: Sale of Equity Shares by Promoters or other significant shareholders may depress the trading price

financial_valuation.detail: Future equity issuances may dilute investors' shareholdings. Any sale of substantial Equity Shares in the public market after the Offer, including by major shareholders, or the perception that such sales could occur, could adversely affect the market price and significantly impair the Company's future ability to raise capital through equity offerings.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Any future equity issuances by our Company may lead to the dilution of investors' shareholdings in our Company.'
financial_valuation.title: Future issuance of Equity Shares may dilute shareholdings and depress the trading price

financial_valuation.detail: Capital gains on sale of Equity Shares are generally taxable in India, with different treatment depending on holding period and whether STT has been paid; gains may be exempt where a treaty between India and the seller's country of residence so provides. Uncertainty exists over the effect of the Finance Bill/Finance Act and the proposed Income Tax Bill, 2025 (which would replace the Income Tax Act, 1961). Buyback proceeds after October 1, 2024 are taxable as dividend with no deduction allowed; dividend distribution tax is not payable on dividends declared after March 31, 2020 and such dividends are taxable in shareholders' hands and likely subject to TDS.
financial_valuation.evidence: Long-term capital gains exceeding the exempted limit of ₹125,000 on listed equity shares taxed at 12.5% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) without indexation; short-term capital gains at 20% (plus surcharge and cess) for transfers after July 23, 2024; gains on shares held more than 12 months are long-term. Stamp duty on transfer of securities other than debentures: 0.015% on delivery basis and 0.003% on non-delivery basis of the consideration amount (Finance Act, 2019 amendment to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 effective July 1, 2020). Finance Bill, 2025 introduced in the Lok Sabha on February 1, 2025.
financial_valuation.title: Investors may be subject to Indian taxes on capital gains from the sale of Equity Shares

financial_valuation.detail: Under Indian law and practice, permission for listing and trading will not be granted until after the Equity Shares have been issued and allotted, and approval requires submission of all relevant documents authorising the issue. There could be a failure or delay in listing the Equity Shares on the BSE SME, which would restrict investors' ability to dispose of their Equity Shares.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'There could be a failure or delay in listing the Equity Shares on the BSE SME.'
financial_valuation.title: No guarantee that the Equity Shares will be listed on BSE SME in a timely manner or at all

financial_valuation.detail: There has been no public market for the Equity Shares prior to the Offer. Trading price may fluctuate due to results of operations and business performance, competitive conditions, general economic, political and social factors, performance of the Indian and global economy, developments in India's fiscal regime, market volatility, competitors' performance, changes in analyst estimates or recommendations, and announcements regarding contracts, acquisitions, strategic partnerships, joint ventures or capital commitments. A loss of investor confidence in the stock markets could depress the price for reasons unrelated to the business, as could events affecting other companies in the industry.
financial_valuation.evidence: SMC Global Securities Limited is acting as Market Maker for the Equity Shares (see 'General Information – Details of the Market Making Arrangement for this Offer', page 67).
financial_valuation.title: Price of the Equity Shares may be volatile and an active trading market may not develop

financial_valuation.detail: The Offer price may not be indicative of the market price after the Offer is completed; investors may not be able to re-sell Equity Shares at or above the Offer price and may lose all or part of their investment. The Equity Shares are expected to trade on the SME Platform of BSE Limited but active trading may not develop or continue, and investors may not be able to sell at the quoted price if trading is not active. Post-Offer price will be determined by the marketplace and influenced by financial condition, results, cash flows, business history and prospects, management assessment, valuation of comparable listed companies, quarterly variations, results versus analyst and competitor expectations, changes in analyst recommendations, acquisition/alliance announcements, announcements of significant claims or proceedings, new laws and regulations, additions or departures of Key Management Personnel, interest rate changes, stock market price and volume fluctuations and general economic conditions. Indian stock markets have experienced significant price and volume fluctuations.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'There has been no public market for our Equity Shares prior to the Offer... Our Equity Shares are expected to trade on the SME Platform of BSE Limited after the Offer.'
financial_valuation.title: Investors bear the risk of price fluctuations and a liquid market may not develop after listing

financial_valuation.detail: The Government of India has traditionally exercised, and continues to exercise, influence over many aspects of the economy. Business and the market price and liquidity of the Equity Shares may be affected by interest rates, changes in Government policy, taxation, social and civil unrest and other political, economic or other developments in or affecting India. The rate of economic liberalisation could change, as could specific laws and policies affecting foreign investment and other matters affecting investment in the Company's securities.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Any significant change in such liberalization and deregulation policies could adversely affect business and economic conditions in India, generally, and our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations, in particular.'
financial_valuation.title: Political instability or changes in economic liberalisation and deregulation policies in India

financial_valuation.detail: Global economic and political factors beyond the Company's control influence forecasts and directly affect performance, including interest rates, rates of economic growth, fiscal and monetary policies of governments, inflation, deflation, foreign exchange fluctuations, consumer credit availability, fluctuations in commodities markets, consumer debt levels, unemployment trends and other matters influencing consumer confidence and spending. Increasing volatility in financial markets may cause these factors to change with greater frequency and magnitude, which may negatively affect the stock price.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Increasing volatility in financial markets may cause these factors to change with a greater degree of frequency and magnitude, which may negatively affect our stock prices.'
financial_valuation.title: Global economic, political and social conditions may harm the business, increase costs and affect the stock price

financial_valuation.detail: Transfers of shares between non-residents and residents are freely permitted (subject to exceptions) only if they comply with RBI pricing guidelines and reporting requirements; otherwise prior RBI approval is required. Shareholders seeking to convert Rupee sale proceeds into foreign currency and repatriate them from India require a no objection/tax clearance certificate from the income tax authority. There is no assurance that any required approval from the RBI or any other government agency can be obtained on any particular terms or at all.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'There can be no assurance that any approval required from the RBI or any other government agency can be obtained on any particular terms or at all.'
financial_valuation.title: Foreign investment restrictions under Indian law limit the ability to attract foreign investors

financial_valuation.detail: Adverse revisions to India's credit ratings for domestic and international debt by international rating agencies may adversely impact the ability to raise additional financing and the interest rates and other commercial terms at which such financing is available, affecting business, future financial performance, the ability to obtain financing for capital expenditure and the trading price of the Equity Shares.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Any adverse revisions to India's credit ratings for domestic and international debt by international rating agencies may adversely impact our ability to raise additional financing.'
financial_valuation.title: Downgrading of India's sovereign rating may harm the ability to raise financing

financial_valuation.detail: Major hostilities involving India or other acts of violence, including civil unrest or similar events beyond the Company's control, could have a material adverse effect on India's economy and on the business. Such incidents may adversely affect the Indian stock markets where the Equity Shares will trade as well as global equity markets, negatively impact business sentiment and trade between countries, and have a material adverse effect on the market for securities of Indian companies.
financial_valuation.evidence: 'Incidents such as the terrorist attacks in India, other incidents such as those in US, Indonesia, Madrid and London, and other acts of violence may adversely affect the Indian stock markets where our Equity Shares will trade as well the global equity markets generally.'
financial_valuation.title: Terrorist attacks, civil unrest and other acts of violence or war

internal_operational.detail: Company manufactures and sells a limited set of hygiene product categories, so financial performance depends disproportionately on continued demand for, and supply of, consumer hygiene products and their raw materials. Adult and baby diapers are recent, immaterial additions. Any disruption in raw material procurement, manufacturing, distribution, or adverse regulatory/pricing developments in this category would hit results directly. A significant proportion of operating expenses is fixed, so unanticipated variations in operations translate into period-to-period volatility in results and cash flows. Diversification of the product portfolio is intended but not assured.
internal_operational.evidence: Sanitary Napkin: ₹12,462.11 lakhs = 95.33% of revenue (Fiscal 2026); ₹9,338.18 lakhs = 81.47% (Fiscal 2025); ₹5,604.72 lakhs = 66.45% (Fiscal 2024). Adult Diaper ₹245.16 lakhs = 1.88% (FY2026), ₹23.73 lakhs = 0.21% (FY2025). Baby diaper ₹35.29 lakhs = 0.27% (FY2026). Total (A) Finished Consumer Goods ₹12,742.56 lakhs = 97.48% (FY2026), ₹9,361.90 lakhs = 81.67% (FY2025), ₹5,604.72 lakhs = 66.45% (FY2024). Own-branded sales were voluntarily slowed in FY2024 and reintroduced in FY2025.
internal_operational.title: Revenue highly concentrated in one product category (sanitary napkins)

internal_operational.detail: The Company has no long-term contract with any customer and no marketing tie-up for its products; supply is on purchase-order basis. Loss of, or interruption of work by, significant customers, or inability to procure new orders, would hit revenue, cash flows and operations. Composition of top customers may change, and any delay or default in payment by these customers would affect the business.
internal_operational.evidence: Fiscal 2026: largest customer ₹6,320.81 lakhs = 48.35% of revenue from operations; top 5 ₹9,166.97 lakhs = 70.13%; top 10 ₹10,511.29 lakhs = 80.41%. Fiscal 2025: ₹3,916.13 lakhs = 34.16%; ₹7,337.74 lakhs = 64.01%; ₹8,976.96 lakhs = 78.32%. Fiscal 2024: ₹2,646.47 lakhs = 31.38%; ₹5,301.86 lakhs = 62.86%; ₹6,711.21 lakhs = 79.57%. 'Our Company neither have any long-term contract with any of customers nor have any marketing tie up for our products.'
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration with no long-term contracts; business done on purchase-order basis

internal_operational.detail: Operations and performance are labour intensive and depend on the ability to identify, attract and retain skilled and unskilled labour. Additional contract labour is hired for specialised jobs or during periods of high customer orders, without any agreement for such hiring, so availability cannot be guaranteed. Strikes, industrial unrest, slowdowns and increased wage costs, and negative publicity from labour unrest, could disrupt operations and harm stakeholder relationships.
internal_operational.evidence: As on May 31, 2026 the Company employed 45 employees, all on its payrolls (including top and middle management, executive directors, manufacturing unit and office staff). No shortage of labour faced in the last three Fiscals and no work disruption due to disputes with the workforce in the three Fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Labour-intensive manufacturing dependent on availability of skilled and unskilled labour; exposure to strikes and wage demands

internal_operational.detail: Business depends on a limited number of suppliers for absorbent polymers, non-woven fabrics, packaging material, chemicals and adhesives. There are no long-term agreements or fixed terms of trade with most suppliers, and favourable credit terms negotiated on the strength of order size and timely payment may not persist. Mitigations cited are supplier performance monitoring, buffer inventories and exploration of additional/alternate domestic suppliers. The Company is also exposed to raw material price fluctuation and to the risk of being unable to pass on cost increases without making products unaffordable.
internal_operational.evidence: Top 10 suppliers contributed around 84.57% (year ended March 31, 2026), 86.86% (March 31, 2025) and 90.50% (March 31, 2024) of purchases.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on a few suppliers for key raw materials, without definitive agreements or fixed terms of trade

internal_operational.detail: A substantial portion of revenue from operations is concentrated in Gujarat. State-specific regulatory changes, new levies, logistics disruption, political or social unrest, natural calamities or weakening economic conditions in the state could disrupt business activities and supply chains. Expansion across multiple states is gradual and there is no assurance it will sufficiently reduce dependence.
internal_operational.evidence: Gujarat revenue: ₹10,067.70 lakhs = 77.02% (Fiscal 2026); ₹8,630.26 lakhs = 75.29% (Fiscal 2025); ₹5,289.86 lakhs = 62.72% (Fiscal 2024) of revenue from operations.
internal_operational.title: Geographic revenue concentration in Gujarat

internal_operational.detail: The business depends on the Rajkot facility, which is subject to shutdowns from equipment or power failure, sub-par output or efficiency, inadequate utilisation, obsolescence, labour disputes, strikes, lockouts, industrial accidents, disruption by extremist groups, and the need to comply with GoI and state government directives. The Company is heavily reliant on floor workers hired on a daily wage / per-piece basis who are not on fixed payroll; loss of such services or disputes with this group could cause under-utilisation of capacity or a total shutdown. Operations involve a significant degree of integration, so results depend on successful operation of each facility.
internal_operational.evidence: 'Our business is dependent on our operating facility in Rajkot, Gujarat. The loss or shutdown of our facilities could have a material adverse effect...'; reliance on 'workers who are hired on a daily wage / per piece basis and are not on a fixed payroll'.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on the single operating facility at Rajkot, Gujarat

internal_operational.detail: While sanitary napkins are made in-house, diapers are manufactured by third-party job-workers, exposing the Company to labour shortages, statutory non-compliance, quality lapses and equipment breakdown at the contract manufacturer's premises, and to deferred dispatches. The engagement is non-exclusive and short-term without a definitive long-term contract; there is no assurance the existing contract manufacturer will continue on timely, cost-effective terms or that alternatives will be available on similar commercial terms. Mitigation is the proposed setting up of the Company's own diaper manufacturing facility.
internal_operational.evidence: 'We are dependent on single contract manufacturer for manufacturing of Diapers'; 'Theis engagement, is on a non-exclusive and short-term basis without definitive long-term contract'; no such instances faced in the last three fiscals; diaper facility referenced under 'Objects of the Offer' on page 87.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on a single contract manufacturer for diapers

internal_operational.detail: The business needs continuous supply of absorbent polymers, non-woven fabrics, packaging material, chemicals and adhesives, and procures certain finished/semi-finished products from third parties. Availability and pricing are subject to quality and availability of supply, changes in consumer demand, changes in government programs, import duties, regulatory restrictions, global commodity price movements, production levels and transportation costs — all beyond the Company's control. Selling-price increases to offset input costs may not be proportionate or sustainable in a highly competitive market.
internal_operational.evidence: Cost of raw materials consumed represented approximately 46.24% (Fiscal 2026), 42.11% (Fiscal 2025) and 46.30% (Fiscal 2024) of revenue from operations. No materially impactful raw-material price rise faced in the last three fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Volatility and disruption in supply and pricing of raw materials and outsourced finished products

internal_operational.detail: The Company relies extensively on third-party transporters for inbound raw materials and for distribution of finished products to CSAs and e-commerce fulfilment centres. Disruption in availability of such services, inadequacies in Indian logistics infrastructure or continuing cost increases could hit the supply chain, production schedules and delivery timelines. Freight is generally borne by the customer but rising costs may not always be passed on. Additional exposures are loss or pilferage in transit, delivery delays and service-provider non-compliance with law. Arrangements with CSAs are based on mutual understanding rather than contract.
internal_operational.evidence: Loading, unloading and transport charges aggregated ₹517.94, ₹459.50 and ₹291.64 representing 4.46%, 4.46% and 3.69% of total expenses for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively. As of May 31, 2026 the Company had partnered with 25 Consignment Selling Agents (CSAs) operating across different states. No such disruption instances faced in the last three fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Reliance on third-party transport, logistics and storage providers and on Consignment Selling Agents

internal_operational.detail: Products are sold through dual channels — distributors and e-commerce platforms — generally without long-term contracts, on purchase orders. Orders may be delayed, changed in scope or quantity, cancelled or not fully paid, affecting production planning and the working capital cycle. Customers can reschedule or cancel at short notice for reasons beyond the Company's control, including their inability to obtain permits or approvals, demand changes, or transportation and warehousing difficulties. Counterparties may also default on payment.
internal_operational.evidence: 'We generally do not execute long-term contracts with our customers and supply our products based on purchase orders.' No such instances materially impacting business operations in the past three fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Customer orders may be delayed, modified, cancelled or not fully paid for

internal_operational.detail: Products are sold through direct-to-business online marketplaces. These marketplaces could change their business practices or seek to modify contractual terms such as payment terms, and may increase the cost of their services due to inflationary pressure or other reasons, adversely affecting expenses and profitability.
internal_operational.evidence: Online channel revenue ₹942.24 lakhs (Fiscal 2026), ₹687.76 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) and ₹419.90 lakhs (Fiscal 2024), representing 7.21%, 6.00% and 4.98% of revenue from operations respectively; platforms named are Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, Snapdeal and Jiomart. No such instances faced in the last three Fiscals.
internal_operational.title: Dependence on online marketplaces and web-traffic drivers for the online sales channel

internal_operational.detail: Results depend on effective inventory management and accurate estimation of customer demand and supply requirements. Misjudging demand causes either product shortages or excess inventory; failure to sell inventory may require disposal, payment to suppliers without new purchases, or additional vendor financing. Overstocking raises capital requirements and financing costs; under-stocking impairs the ability to meet demand. Natural disasters and extreme weather may disrupt supply and local transportation with no assurance of an alternate source in time.
internal_operational.evidence: Inventory ₹4,623.25 lakhs (Fiscal 2026), ₹2,588.79 lakhs (Fiscal 2025), ₹3,232.64 lakhs (Fiscal 2024). The 'Inventory holding days' row is presented in the table without values. No past instances of delivery disruption from poor handling or transportation bottlenecks.
internal_operational.title: Inability to accurately forecast demand and manage inventory

internal_operational.detail: Profitability depends on optimising production and capacity utilisation. Disruptions at the manufacturing facility — labour unrest, unexpected events, temporary scheduled maintenance or inability to procure sufficient raw materials — could cause operational inefficiencies affecting actual production, capacity utilisation and sales. The Company proposes a brownfield expansion to capitalise on anticipated industry growth, with no assurance of an immediate or any increase in revenue.
internal_operational.evidence: Fully Servo Sanitary Pad Making Machine-1: actual production 11.13 crore pcs, capacity utilisation 92.75% (FY2025-26); 10.24 crore pcs, 85.33% (FY2024-25); 11.40 crore pcs, 95.00% (FY2023-24). Fully Servo Sanitary Napkin Making Machine-2: capacity 8 crore pcs, production 7.02 crore pcs, 87.75% (FY2025-26); 8 crore pcs per annum, 6.83 crore pcs, 85.38% (FY2024-25); not applicable FY2023-24. Note: the new machinery line was installed on 31 March 2024 and commenced full-scale production in FY2024-25. No instances of under-utilisation in Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024.
internal_operational.title: Under-utilisation of existing production lines and inability to utilise expanded capacity

internal_operational.detail: Success depends in part on effective, timely and cost-effective deployment of IT systems. Computer networks may be vulnerable to unauthorised access, hacking, viruses, worms, malicious applications and other security problems caused by improper use of systems by employees, subcontractors or third-party vendors. A breach releasing user data could harm reputation and brand and expose the Company to legal liability, penalties, negative publicity, forced changes to business practices and increased costs.
internal_operational.evidence: 'While we have not faced any such failure in the past three fiscals...'
internal_operational.title: IT system failures or employee lapses causing operational interruption, liability or reputational harm

internal_operational.detail: Products may contain quality issues or undetected errors or defects — especially when first introduced or newly developed — arising from design, manufacture or raw materials. Quality control processes and inspections of supplier and contract-manufacturer raw materials and finished goods may fail or be inaccurate. Shortcomings due to failure of quality assurance procedures, negligence or human error may damage products and the quality certificate, and result in deficient products.
internal_operational.evidence: Facility holds ISO 9001:2015 and WHO-GMP certification and a BIS certification. 'We experience sales returns regularly in our normal course of business.'
internal_operational.title: Failure in quality control processes

internal_operational.detail: The business and industry are subject to vendor/dealer/employee fraud, theft or embezzlement and to product pilferage. Security measures cited are deployment of supervisors, periodic stock taking, relevant insurance and entitlement to recover shortages from employees, but there is no assurance against future fraud, theft, employee negligence or loss in transit, or of successful insurance claims. Employee misconduct or errors could expose the Company to regulatory sanctions, negligence claims and reputational harm, and precautions may not be effective in all cases.
internal_operational.evidence: 'While there have been no certain instances where our employees have engaged in pilferage of our products.'
internal_operational.title: Fraud, theft or embezzlement by employees or the contract manufacturer, and employee misconduct or errors

internal_operational.detail: As the Company expands, success depends on effective use of resources and maintenance of internal controls; financial and management control processes and compliance procedures may need modification to meet evolving business needs. If controls, systems and procedures are not improved they may become ineffective, and efforts to improve internal control systems may not eliminate all risks, including operational errors and incidents of fraud.
internal_operational.evidence: No instances of failure of internal controls having a material adverse effect on business in Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024.
internal_operational.title: Failure or significant weakness of the internal controls system

internal_operational.detail: Success largely depends on the knowledge and experience of the Promoters, Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management, and on the ability to attract and retain skilled personnel. The Company depends on Promoter guidance for business strategy development, monitoring implementation and meeting future challenges. Replacement of technically skilled personnel may require a long period to hire and train, and compensation may need to rise faster than in the past to remain competitive. There is significant competition for management and skilled personnel in the industry.
internal_operational.evidence: 'Any loss of our Promoter, Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management or our ability to attract and retain them and other skilled personnel could adversely affect our business...' (see 'Our Management', page 161).
internal_operational.title: Dependence on Promoters, Directors, KMP and Senior Management and on retaining technically skilled personnel

internal_operational.detail: Governments including India imposed country-wide lockdowns and restrictions on travel and business operations; most measures were lifted from May 2020. Further lockdowns could have significant additional effects on revenue, financial condition and results. Uncertainties include the number of individuals infected, availability of a vaccine or cure, the extent of protective measures imposed by governments and whether the virus's impact will be seasonal. Inadequate response, or customer perception of inadequate response, could damage reputation and brand.
internal_operational.evidence: COVID-19 recognised as a pandemic by the WHO on March 11, 2020; lockdown re-imposed in some parts of India during April 2021 and partially relaxed in June 2021, during which period 'our stores were partially operational'.

internal_operational.detail: India's physical infrastructure is in a developing phase compared to many developed nations. strategy_growth.detail: The hygiene and personal care industry is characterised by rapidly evolving consumer preferences, product innovation and changing lifestyle and health awareness trends, with consumers increasingly demanding products that are safe, effective, convenient and environmentally sustainable. The Company addresses these trends through its brand portfolio and continuous investment in product innovation and marketing, but there is no assurance these efforts will be sufficient or timely. Failure to anticipate or respond could reduce demand, cause loss of market share or diminish brand loyalty.
strategy_growth.evidence: Brands: Femiss, Womanica, ElderFit and Bloom Baby. 'the market is projected to expand further, reaching USD 3,463.86 million by 2032' — growth factors cited are improved rural access, expanding e-commerce penetration, demand for sustainable alternatives, increasing participation of women in the workforce, evolving lifestyles and a growing elderly population (Source: Credence Research Report).
strategy_growth.title: Inability to timely adapt to changing consumer preferences, spending patterns and hygiene/personal care trends

strategy_growth.detail: The reputation, recognition and goodwill of the Company's brands are central to differentiating products, attracting and retaining customers and distributors and sustaining market position, and a significant portion of growth and visibility is attributable to acceptance and perceived quality of branded products. Brand equity may be impaired by lapses in maintaining requisite statutory approvals and quality standards; sale of counterfeit, look-alike or unauthorised products by third parties; unsatisfactory service levels or non-compliance by distributors or dealers positioning themselves as authorised partners; adverse media or unfavourable social-media commentary, including by influencers and public figures not engaged by the Company; and actual or perceived breaches of customer data privacy or cyber-security incidents. Allegations of product defects, product recalls or negative publicity may still occur despite internal policies and quality checks.
strategy_growth.evidence: Brands marketed: Femiss, Womanica, ElderFit and Bloom Baby. 'While we have not face such instances in the last 3 Fiscals, there can be no assurance that such measures will be effective at all times.'
strategy_growth.title: Brands and reputation are critical assets and any deterioration could hurt the business

strategy_growth.detail: Historical growth has been driven in significant part by the ability to acquire new customers and deepen relationships with existing ones, but there is no assurance that historical growth rates can be maintained, that new customers can be attracted on a continuing basis or at all, or that existing customers will continue purchasing in the same quantities or frequencies. Maintaining and expanding the customer base requires sustained marketing and promotional investment, which may increase due to heightened competition for consumer attention and digital traffic, changing consumer preferences, or higher media and promotional costs. If conversion rates are lower than anticipated, customer acquisition costs may become disproportionate to revenue generated, hurting margins and profitability; retention and growth may also require increased advertising and promotional expenditure or incentives and discounts beyond current expectations.
strategy_growth.evidence: Served more than 227 customers for the financial years ended March 31, 2024 to March 31, 2026. Revenue from operations increased from ₹8,434.76 lakhs (FY2024) to ₹11,462.56 lakhs (FY2025) and further to ₹13,072.09 lakhs (FY2026). For the financial year ended March 31, 2026, marketing and advertising expenses were ₹579.14 lakhs, representing 4.43% of revenue from operations and 4.99% of total expenses.
strategy_growth.title: Failure to acquire new consumers, or to do so cost-effectively

strategy_growth.detail: No firm purchase orders have been placed for the capital expenditure proposed towards purchase and installation of new equipment and machinery and construction of the manufacturing facility. Until orders are finalised, delivery timelines, pricing and specifications of the machinery remain uncertain. Delays may arise from prolonged supplier negotiations, changes in design or specifications, or supply chain constraints affecting vendors. Even after orders are placed, exposures remain to late delivery, defects in supplied machinery, installation delays, non-availability of skilled personnel for installation, and cost escalation — any of which could postpone or disrupt planned capacity expansion and operations and increase project costs.
strategy_growth.evidence: 'We have not yet placed firm purchase orders for the capital expenditure proposed to be incurred towards the purchase and installation of new equipment and machinery and construction of manufacturing facility.'
strategy_growth.title: Orders for the proposed capital expenditure on equipment/machinery and construction of the manufacturing facility have not yet been placed

strategy_growth.detail: Products and packaging are visible to a large number of consumers and competitors, exposing the Company to unfair trade practices including manufacture and sale of counterfeit, cloned, look-alike and pass-off products. Imitation can extend to brand names, packaging, colour schemes, trade dress and other distinctive features. Such products may divert sales from genuine products and create heightened reputation risk; they are often sold at lower prices and may be of inferior quality, potentially harming consumers and eroding trust in the brands. Management time and resources may be diverted to pursue claims, complaints or litigation, and there is no assurance all instances can be detected, prevented or addressed in a timely or cost-effective manner.
strategy_growth.evidence: 'In the past, we have not experienced incidents of such practices.'
strategy_growth.title: Exposure to unfair competitive or trade practices — counterfeit, cloned, look-alike and pass-off products

strategy_growth.detail: Growth strategies require developing and strengthening relationships with existing customers who may drive high-volume orders on an ongoing basis, increasing business from existing customers, adding new customers and expanding into new geographical markets. Success may be affected by the ability to maintain product quality, increase geographic presence, the general condition of the global economy (particularly India and other markets of operation), the ability to compete effectively with existing and future competitors, and changes in the Indian or international regulatory environment — many of which are beyond the Company's control. There is no assurance strategies can be executed on time and within estimated budget, or that expansion and development plans will increase profitability. Growth strategies are expected to place significant demands on management, financial and other resources and require continued development of operational, financial and other internal controls.
